messages:
alex: @maria escalate pls — Acme (enterprise) says ~30d TTL objects are still visible after 45d. Customer provided object IDs and a screen cap. They also saw KMS errors around the time of expected deletion: 

alex: sample object ids: obj_8a7f, obj_8a80, obj_8b01
alex: repro steps they ran: 
```bash
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/objects/obj_8a7f\"
# returns 200 with object metadata including ttl: 2025-06-01T12:00:00Z
```

maria: thanks — can you drop the exact IDs and the customer request id? I will open a support ticket and triage with infra. Any audit-log entries for deletion attempts?

alex: ticket id CS-3281. we've got these auditlog snippets from their side: 
```
2025-06-02T12:01:03Z delete-request obj_8a7f user:svc-acme result: accepted request_id: rq_77
2025-06-02T12:01:04Z storage.delete.enqueue obj_8a7f status: queued
2025-06-02T12:01:06Z kms.decrypt obj_key_8a7f error: HSM-403 key not found
2025-06-02T12:01:06Z storage.delete.fail obj_8a7f reason: key-unavailable
```

support-bot: Created escalation CS-3281-Escalation and linked to INC-8852 — support runbook: https://internal/runbooks/retention-kms-issues :thumbsup: 

sam-eng: looking. This reads like the deletion pipeline attempted but failed to unwrap object key because of a key rotation/republish race. Possible flow: KMS rotated, key metadata not propagated to storage, deletion path treats unavailable key as non-deletable and extends retention. We need to check our deletion-backoff job and key-sync.

alex: I dug up additional logs from customer showing a KMS rotation window at 2025-06-02T11:59:50Z with HSM logs showing: 
```
HSM: rotate_key key_id:k_2025_06_02 status: success
HSM: replicate_key key_id:k_2025_06_02 target:zone-b status: pending
HSM: decrypt key_id:k_old error: key-not-found (ERR_HSM_KEY_MISSING)
```

legal-jd: Legal asks we PAUSE any automatic purge for this customer until we confirm no data was inadvertently preserved. Also they requested export of deletion audit trail by EOD. Please mark legal-hold if we cannot confirm deletion.

sam-eng: proposed workaround to get customer data into compliant state without waiting for the backfill: run a targeted admin purge that uses the service KMS key to unwrap, then force-delete objects. This requires ops approval and will leave an explicit audit entry. Example admin command (internal only):
```bash
redwood-admin purge --project acme --object obj_8a7f --service-key-file /secrets/service-key.pem --force --reason \"urgent-customer-purge KMS-rotation-failure\"
```

maria: we need SRE/KMS on-call to approve and run. Also confirm that purge writes audit entries to retention.audit and to the tenant's audit log for legal. @sam-eng do you have the minimal set of logs we should capture?

sam-eng: yes — capture: delete-request, storage.delete.enqueue, kms.decrypt attempts, kms.rotate events, storage.delete.success/fail, and the admin-purge invocation and response. I'll attach a checklist: 
- gather those logs from time window 2025-06-02T11:58:00 -> 2025-06-02T12:05:00
- snapshot object metadata (headers+versions)
- run admin purge with --force and capture stdout/stderr + HTTP request/response bodies

alex: customer gave approval for forced purge and wants us to proceed. They also asked for a manual verification step once objects are gone.

ops-runbook: I kicked off INC-8852 and pinged KMS on-call (pagerduty). Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/retention-kms-issues — follow section "admin purge with audit". I scheduled the purge for 2025-06-02T16:30:00Z to allow legal time to review.

maria: thanks. I'll update CS-3281 with the plan, include legal and CSM loop, and request SRE to run the purge at scheduled time. Please attach the logs after the run so legal can audit.

sam-eng: will run purge at scheduled time, attach logs to CS-3281 and INC-8852, and start a short-postmortem draft highlighting: race between key-rotation replication and deletion worker + gap in audit entries for retried deletes. Postmortem ETA: 48h.
